speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We are creating GovTech from the strong foundation that IDA and its predecessor, the National Computer Board (NCB), have built.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: GovTech has vast experience in managing enterprise information technology (IT) systems for the public sector and implementing service-wide e-services, such as Singpass, OneInbox and the OneService mobile app.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Technological advances are constantly disrupting our operating environment and the public's expectations of Government services are rising.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: At the same time, technological advances in ICT and related engineering create new opportunities for the Government to deliver innovative and impactful digital services to citizens and businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: GovTech will play an important role in driving the digital transformation of the public sector, with citizens at the centre.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: GovTech will work with agencies to try new things, test ideas, commission proof of concepts, and take calculated risks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: At the same time, GovTech will further build on the core of its work to develop and maintain systems, as well as to ensure that the Government's ICT systems remain reliable, secure and are safe against cyber threats.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: GovTech will drive the Government's delivery of the next generation of citizen-centric, anticipatory and secure digital services to individuals, businesses and public sector employees.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: When developing these services, GovTech will implement industry best practices, such as agile development, emphasis on user interface design and the use of data analytics.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: GovTech will also encourage citizen participation in co-creating applications that can benefit the public.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It will do so by making data and other tools, such as Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), open and publicly available.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: An example is the Beeline app that brings together private bus operators and commuters with common transport routes and uses EZ-link data to assess demand for suggested routes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Instead of the Government developing all services for citizens, GovTech aims to build platforms that facilitate greater co-creation with citizens and 	Page: 133 businesses, and engender a culture of crowd-sourcing.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We believe that there are many other innovative apps waiting to be co-created that will benefit the public.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: As a leading competency centre of ICT and related engineering capability within the Government, GovTech will be well-placed to support Singapore's Smart Nation vision.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: GovTech will take the lead to put in place the underlying public sector infrastructure needed to operate a Smart Nation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: One example is providing the infrastructure and data analytics backbone to support sensors deployed by public sector agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: GovTech will ensure that the deployment of such sensors by the public sector is well-coordinated and optimised.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It will also promote the sharing of sensors and sensor data among agencies to maximise their usefulness.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Another example is an effort with the Singapore Land Authority and National Research Foundation (NRF) to develop a Virtual 3D geospatial rendering of Singapore to aid in urban planning and operations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It is also critical that GovTech ensures the reliability and security of our ICT systems across the public sector.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It will put in place strong technical standards, clear governing policies and robust security measures for a resilient ICT infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This will apply across all public sector agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Given the interconnectedness of our ICT applications and networks, the strength of the entire system depends on the weakest link.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Therefore, where necessary, GovTech will be actively involved in the governance of public sector ICT systems, regardless of whether they are managed directly by GovTech or by their own in-house IT teams.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Rather, they allow agencies to innovate with the confidence that they are building their systems on the foundation of robust security and resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: To do all of the above well, GovTech will need to sustain deep technical capabilities in ICT and software development, as well as to build new ones.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: These capabilities extend beyond the ICT domain, and include related engineering fields, such as the Internet of Things, or fields which have become essential to the delivery of digital experiences, such as design.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: GovTech will set up Capability Centres to focus on developing technical specialists in these fields.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Examples include application development, data science, Government ICT infrastructure, geospatial technology, cybersecurity and sensors, and the Internet of Things.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: GovTech will recruit ICT professionals, both fresh out of school and mid-career professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: There are already programmes, such as the Technology Associates Programme (TAP) and the Smart Nation Fellowship Programme, to attract talent to work at GovTech.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: GovTech will also foster an organisational culture of experimentation, inclusivity and learning that empowers our people to be bold about how they can make a positive difference.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: GovTech will primarily work within the public sector.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In anticipation of future developments in technology, including in the fields of cyber-physical systems and the Internet of Things, GovTech's remit in the Bill goes beyond ICT to include "related engineering" areas.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: I will now highlight the key clauses in the Bill itself.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Parts 1 and 2 of the Bill provide for the key definitions used in the Bill and to establish GovTech.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Page: 134 Parts 3 to 6 relate to the formation of GovTech's Board, the decision-making procedures, personnel and financial matters.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: GovTech will be able to develop, implement and monitor the agencies' compliance with directives, codes, standards or guidelines.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It can carry out audits and report on agencies' non-compliance, including the power to require access to information or premises.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: If authorised by the Minister, GovTech can direct agencies to implement security, mitigation or recovery measures that it considers necessary from a security or reliability standpoint, including the deployment of resources and personnel.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: After this Bill is passed, GovTech will provide agencies with administrative details on how these powers will be implemented.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: These are called "public entities" in the Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: An example is restructured hospitals, which, although not part of the public sector, are nonetheless an essential part in the delivery of public healthcare.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The intent is certainly not to take over the running of IT systems of such public entities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: However, if the info-comms or related engineering systems or service of a public entity is at significant risk or has been significantly compromised, or if it is in the public interest to do so, it would be sub-optimal if GovTech, with its capabilities, is unable to assist in any way.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Hence, the Bill provides that under certain specified conditions, GovTech may develop and recommend directives, codes, standards or guidelines, as well as to provide advice on security, mitigation or recovery measures.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The Bill contains clear conditions and safeguards under which GovTech can assist public entities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Once a request is made, the Minister for Communications and Information will assess and may direct GovTech to establish the necessary arrangements with the public entity.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: GovTech will have to seek the public entity's agreement on the scope of the governance measures and the manner in which GovTech's measures and standards will be applicable.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This arrangement must also be approved by the "Responsible Minister", who remains accountable for the public entity's execution of the necessary actions and compliance to GovTech's recommendations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Parts 9 to 11 of the Bill relate to the administration within GovTech that provides for offences under the Bill, the transfer of undertakings and personnel of IDA to GovTech, and saving and transitional arrangements.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The formation of GovTech enables the Government to deepen its capabilities in ICT and related engineering fields and attract engineering talent into these areas.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Prof Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: GovTech will allow the Government to deepen our technical capabilities and enable us to remain agile and responsive to leverage technology in making a difference to the lives of our citizens and businesses.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It aims to deliver citizen-centric services to support Singapore's Smart Nation vision by pushing the boundaries in the use of applied technology and levelling up the ICT standards in Government.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In this expansion of its mandate alone, the very establishment of GovTech is designed to innovate governance here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And we are probably the first government in the world that announced an agency focusing on Government technology.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This focus should enable GovTech to lead the Singapore Government's innovation of its processes, offerings, functions, infrastructure and citizen engagement.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But we must not forget that the ultimate goal is to improve citizens' lives and make governance more productive for their benefit.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We can do more to make Government technology inclusive for all.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Some of the applications that IDA currently deploys show promise.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Like the Minister described earlier, MyInfo service allows citizens, who have given their personal details before, to have their transaction forms online pre-filled upon their consent.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The MyResponder app by the Singapore Civil Defence Force is one example, which links cardiac arrest patients to nearby volunteers to help save lives.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Third, I hope that GovTech can bring the whole of Government with it to unlock the value of information to solve everyday problems affecting citizens.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Beeline is one such example, which analyses user-suggested route data with existing transport data smartly to identify popular routes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Besides the development of efficiency and innovation within society, I hope that GovTech will also continue to play an important role in protecting our Government systems and citizen data which are stored in these systems.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: With all these functions, GovTech will be the core technology agency within the Government.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, this role will also require it to work closely with other agencies in areas that are, at present, cross-cutting or overlapping.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is less clear how this will be done and if any of the functions will be reassigned to GovTech instead or what permutations may exist.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Minister covered several restrictions in the Bill, outlining GovTech's ability to work with other agencies or advise the private sector, for example, the oil industry.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: With GovTech developing expertise and experience handling complex ICT projects for the public sector, it has a lot of potential to also help the private sector and the industries.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Should the work of GovTech extend beyond the current scope of mainly operating within the public sector?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For example, can GovTech share expertise and Government experience in cybersecurity and analytics and help the SMEs, for example?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Conversely, there is a lot that GovTech can learn from and collaborate with the private sector.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am not sure if the Minister plays Pokemon Go!, but I know many Singaporeans who have.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am not at a very high level, but I keep up with my kids and to understand the phenomenon.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But what this app has achieved, as several Members have spoken before me, it is through innovation of what agencies like the National Parks Board and the National Heritage Board would have benefited.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For example, today, you have more Singaporeans going on heritage trails and going to our parks, for example, which we have difficulty getting people to do before this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And today, the Health Promotion Board should also thank Pokemon Go! for the many kilometres our digital-natives are walking through just to hatch Pokemon eggs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There is a symbiosis that we can tap and much potential that can be synergised through the exchange of ideas, research and collaboration.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Whether or not GovtTech's scope extends beyond the public sector, it is also important to put in place various indicators to determine if GovTech is heading the nation in the right direction as many of its functions can be difficult to evaluate.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As the building of Singapore into a Smart Nation is an important exercise that we cannot get wrong, how do we know if we are in the right direction?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, what will be GovTech's measure of success?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Do we measure it based on how many citizen-centric apps are created to improve engagement with society?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Or do we measure its success based on how efficient or productive the Government becomes in offering its services to the people?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But based on how wide GovTech's mandate is, there are certainly many other possible measures and these will have to be decided upon.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Malay):   The establishment of GovTech is a welcome move in view of the many changes that have occurred in the global technology landscape.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It will definitely approach the application of technology in a way that will further benefit our citizens and our nation, operating under the concept and implementation of a Smart Nation vision.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Technology is now widely used but education and upskilling will be required from time to time.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What is also important is that, hopefully, as many people as possible will be comfortable using technology in their dealings with the Government, including in terms of cybersecurity.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For 	Page: 137 instance, websites, apps, electronic transactions and others should be easy and safe to use, including in terms of data security.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I rise in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, GovTech will do so in a very different context, one where ICT has become pervasive and is, in many cases, mission-critical in the Civil Service.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: GovTech looks set to take the lead in enabling the public sector to optimally use big data analytics, artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things and other disruptive technologies.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It will probably take the lead in the procurement of IT systems for the public sector.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is also likely to play a leading role in setting and enforcing best practice standards as well as levelling up the standards of public sector agencies in terms of their use of ICT to fulfil their missions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As such, the role of GovTech is potentially very impactful.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In other developed countries, SMEs have the advantage of good access to their domestic market, an advantage that some of our SMEs and local enterprises lack due to the small size of our domestic market.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is compounded by the fact that many public sector agencies may tend to prefer established global brands in procuring ICT systems and services.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These local champions should be our economy's strong third pillar of job creation and value creation, a pillar that will hopefully be more resilient and rooted to Singapore whichever way global economic winds blow, as compared to multinational corporations.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Page: 138 No doubt Singapore needs to observe its obligations under the Government Procurement Agreement (GPA), which requires non-discrimination against foreign firms.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, there could be ways to work with local firms while remaining consistent with the GPA.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, GovTech could work with certain local firms with niche technologies on R&D partnerships which are not procurement tenders per se.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Such local firms could also receive targeted SME incentives from economic promotion agencies like SPRING Singapore or the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR).

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Another possibility is to issue certain procurement tenders that provide preferential consideration for SMEs, both local and foreign.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This may, in certain context, be GPA-compliant, if the same preference is given to both local and foreign SMEs.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But practically speaking, of course, there will not be as much foreign SME competition as there would be foreign MNC competition.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Some global government agencies, I am given to understand, do implement SME preferences in their tender evaluation criteria to some degree in this way.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I hope that the Ministry of Communications and Information and GovTech will consider such approaches.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I would urge GovTech to give serious thought to this because not only would it result in greater privacy protection, such regular private investment assessments (PIAs) would also help strengthen public confidence in sharing information with Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: PIAs are conducted by first world government agencies such as the Pentagon and Department of Homeland Security in the United States and the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) in the United Kingdom (UK), for example.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thirdly, the Civil Service, including all Statutory Boards and agencies, is a vast organisation.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Across the ranks of all state employees, there could exist a digital divide, with some employees being much more IT-literate in their skills and habits than others, particularly including some of those who are older.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I suggest that GovTech take the lead in identifying IT literacy gaps within the broader Civil Service and use its considerable procurement power to develop and push out ICT literacy training on a whole-of-Government basis.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This would enable those state employees who are lagging in comfort level in ICT skills to level up and thus gain access to productivity-enhancing opportunities which would improve their career prospects.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: With the creation of GovTech, would not GovTech offer the best location for the lead agency for public sector cyber security?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Are there plans for the CSA to thus eventually be subsumed under GovTech?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This would facilitate cybersecurity becoming better embedded in public sector ICT systems, processes and cultures.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If the answer to that question is that CSA is tasked with national level cybersecurity going beyond just the public sector, should it not then be located under the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) which would allow better integration with other modalities of Total Defence?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: GovTech has a huge task at hand, not only because of the scale of supporting 90-plus Government agencies, but also because it ventures into the unknown with technology and needs constantly evolving.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What then will be GovTech's measure of success?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Consumers now find themselves faced with a dazzling array of card payment terminals with proprietary standards when they want to make payments.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: And credit card payments are already graduating towards mobile-enabled payments.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We are thus in need of a platform that enables a seamless payment experience for consumers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This not only provides greater convenience to consumers but can also increase productivity and cut down costs for businesses.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: For instance, the man-hours and costs of processing cheques and handling cash are far higher than those of processing digital payments.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, a corollary of progressing mobile and digital payments is the ability to authenticate one's digital identity.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While we are moving towards two-factor authentication for Singpass, huge advances are already being made in biometric authentication for financial services.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Biometric automated teller machines have been deployed in several parts of the world including the UK, Japan, China, Brazil and Poland.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given Singapore's limited resources, the general economic climate and evolving trends in business models, there is an increasing need for us to embrace a "sharing model" to deploy resources more effectively.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: There are many latent resources in our society and community.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This could be in the form of physical assets, labour and capital, for instance, under-utilised community spaces, stay-at-home mums who could act as volunteers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: If GovTech is able to co-create solutions with citizens to enable better use of latent resources in our society, we could have win-win solutions for owners of resources and society as a whole.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Separately, for special needs communities or the elderly, technology can be used to enable the elderly and less physically abled to access Government services from home, work from home and be more productive.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This would help build a more inclusive society as more segments of the 	Page: 140 population can be actively participating in societal developments.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Those with disabilities can also potentially use their abilities to support themselves, enabled by smart devices to help them operate equipment, read and also enter data.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: GovTech could thus be a key enabler in society, using technology to build platforms and creating convenience and increasing convenience for consumers as well as raise productivity for industries.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: GovTech could also be a key mobiliser in society, using technology to access segments of the population that are underserved and unleash the potentials in them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I hope the Ministry is able to prioritise the work of GovTech to maximise its role and make a critical difference to the lives of citizens.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In our electronic global village, cybersecurity is of the utmost concern.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Although a large proportion of these attacks are cybercrimes targeted at siphoning money from corporations and individuals, there were also cases of cyber espionage and cyber warfare targeted at Government systems.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In today's electronic day and age, a successful attack on our e-Government system will have widespread social and economic impact on our nation.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The fallout from such an attack could be likened to the detonation of a cyber-nuclear bomb, leading to a long nuclear winter in cyberspace where the Government system would be paralysed for a sustained period of time.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While there are obvious advantages of adopting a centralised Government-wide cybersecurity framework, it also means that the impact of a successful intrusion will increase exponentially, since intruders can now exploit the same backdoor that exists in the entire e-Government system.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe that it is thus imperative for GovTech to explicate clearly how it will work hand in hand with CSA and perhaps other agencies to enhance cybersecurity across the different Government entities.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Most importantly, GovTech needs to ensure its own gates are secure because it now holds the master key, as it were, to our e-Government system.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Two examples I can think of are in the public transport and public healthcare areas.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Page: 141 Although co-operation in these areas are with private organisations that are currently outside the official public sector framework, they provide essential services to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I believe that it is thus in the public interest that GovTech work very closely with corporations in such areas as developing actionable intelligence by using big data analytics techniques so that these corporations can better predict usage patterns of their service and design more consumer-centric service delivery models.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: GovTech should also work with these private corporations to ensure that their cybersecurity systems are not compromised, as that would have a negative impact on the public and society at large.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In such an environment, the Government will no doubt continue to offer more citizen-centric online platforms for Singaporeans to interact with the various public agencies.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And as these platforms emerge and evolve, we also need to ensure that we have a robust network and security system to support these e-services.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It will pave the way for Singapore to go full speed ahead as a Smart Nation, providing top-class infrastructure for people and businesses to thrive.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I especially welcome this move towards co-creation with the community, as I believe the Government does not hold the monopoly on good ideas and innovations, especially not with the growing pool of exceptional talent among the youths.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Furthermore, as interactions with Government services move increasingly to the digital realm, the move to streamline IT-related transactions can only serve Singaporeans better.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many of my older and less tech-savvy residents in Nee Soon East face challenges navigating the complex web of Government red tape when trying to apply for licences, grants, social welfare services, and so on.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This committee will further strengthen our move towards co-creation with the community.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Page: 142 Based on my experience as part of the Animal Welfare Legislation Review Committee, which led to improvements in animal welfare policies and legislation, I have found great value in setting up committees which include parties with differing views.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For example, the Animal Welfare Legislation Review Committee comprised of Members of Parliament, animal welfare groups, Town Council staff, veterinarians and the pet industry.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was a group of stakeholders with diverse views, who are not like-minded at times, but came together to argue, debate and find common ground.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I strongly believe that it is committees like these, with more devil's advocates, where we will get the best policies drafted and, in this case, the best technology created.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The robust debates among people with dissenting views will ensure that we truly understand what the ground concerns and the various ideas out there are, and the different solutions available.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Because ultimately, I believe we do not have all the answers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These comments notwithstanding, Sir, I stand in support of the Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: First, Ms Sun Xueling and Mr Zaqy Mohamad both asked about what success would look like for GovTech.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I had earlier spoken about GovTech's role in driving the digital transformation of the public sector and in partnering Government agencies to deliver next-generation digital services to the public.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Citizens desire the same level of efficiency and personalisation from public services that they receive from digital services they use in other spheres of their life.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: GovTech is cognisant of this rising public expectation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For example, GovTech is reviewing how technology can better enable public services to be more personalised and anticipatory when individuals and businesses interact with the Government, such as registering a marriage, buying a flat or applying for licences.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I also agree with the broader points that Ms Sun Xueling and Mr Louis Ng have made, which is that GovTech should consult more widely and, as far as possible, co-create with and crowd source from the community in the implementation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: GovTech will work closely with the respective lead Government agencies to do so, with a view towards designing and delivering more citizen-centric digital services.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Beeline and MyResponder applications are examples of how digital services can be designed to enable citizens to play a more active role in achieving more impactful outcomes for the larger community.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: At the same time, GovTech will continually benchmark ourselves against international best practices to ensure that we remain a leading digital government in the world.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Page: 143 On this note, I would like to thank Ms Sun Xueling for her suggestion that GovTech should look into the development of more efficient electronic payments in Singapore, in light of developments in this area abroad.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: IDA is already working with the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), the Ministry of Finance (MOF) and key industry players to effect the shift towards digital payments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: While GovTech harnesses technological advances in ICT to drive innovation and the digital transformation of Government services, it is also critical that there is adequate focus on its core work, which is to keep the public sector ICT systems stable, secure and resilient.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I echo Mr Darryl David's concern that it is an area which we cannot take for granted, given the increased risk of cybersecurity breaches and rapidly evolving cyber threat landscape.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: At the end of the day, we are cognisant that GovTech's goal must be to improve the lives of Singapore Citizens.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I agree with Ms Sun Xueling that technology can be a key enabler in our society.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The Government is committed to ensuring that all groups have access to and can benefit from technology.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Today, IDA and MDA have a wide range of programmes that support vulnerable groups in society, such as the elderly, disabled persons and school-going children from low-income households, through initiatives, such as the Silver Infocomm Initiative.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: We aim to build a culture of co-creation between citizens and businesses through open data and application programming interfaces or APIs, which can unleash the untapped potential in the population.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, we welcome citizens from all backgrounds to provide ideas and develop applications using these APIs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The overarching principle is that GovTech will coordinate closely with these agencies and tap on one another's expertise and experience.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In some cases, like DSTA, the scope of its work is quite distinctly different from GovTech's, whereas, with other agencies, we can expect more collaboration.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In the area of cybersecurity, CSA is the authority at the national level spanning 11 sectors to ensure that critical information infrastructures are resilient and protected from cyber threats.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: GovTech will oversee cybersecurity for one of these sectors – the Government sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Leon Perera has a specific question on why CSA is sited in PMO instead of MINDEF.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is to give CSA the ability to oversee cybersecurity at the national level because there are 11 critical sectors in which cybersecurity measures have to be put in place to protect the critical ICT systems.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For the Government sector, the responsibility rests on GovTech, which will work closely with CSA to ensure that we put in place the necessary measures, as stipulated by CSA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It should benefit from the pipeline of research from the research institutes in 	Page: 144 Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Hence, it will collaborate with agencies in this domain, such as the NRF and A*STAR.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Members also asked about GovTech's role in the Smart Nation initiative vis-a-vis SNPO.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Like many other agencies that contribute to the Smart Nation vision, GovTech will work closely with SNPO, which will coordinate agencies' efforts towards the Smart Nation vision.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: GovTech plays a key role in implementing the Digital Government strategy, which is a key plank in the Smart Nation vision.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: GovTech will lead the public sector effort to design and implement Government ICT infrastructure and digital services, including the Smart Nation platform, in order to deliver innovative citizen-centric solutions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad and Mr Darryl David have asked if GovTech's work should extend beyond the current scope of mainly operating within the public sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I would, first of all, like to thank both Members for their votes of confidence, but GovTech cannot and should not do everything.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It should focus on the digital transformation efforts in the public sector and support the development of Smart Nation, which is already a very significant task.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: GovTech will work closely with the newly-formed IMDA on its industry-development efforts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: For example, GovTech will support IMDA's accreditation programme to accredit promising Singapore-based ICT startups and bring innovative products to Government agencies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Mr Leon Perera has some suggestions on how we can work with SMEs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: This effort will be continued by IMDA, working together with GovTech.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I would also like to emphasise that even as GovTech builds deeper technical capabilities, it will not be able to design, develop and maintain ICT systems and applications by itself.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Public sector projects and solutions are often co-created with private sector partners in ways that are mutually beneficial.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The private sector has skills and strengths that can complement what GovTech does well, which GovTech does not intend to compete or displace.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: At the same time, GovTech's work will definitely have an impact on both the wider ICT industry, due to the scale and variety of the Government's technology needs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: GovTech can spur the industry by acting as a catalyst for progressive and interesting public sector ICT initiatives and projects.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: By uplifting ICT technology standards in the Government, GovTech can also ensure high standards in industry and influence the direction of investment and growth in our ICT sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: It is in GovTech's interest that there is a vibrant ICT industry ecosystem, comprising both smaller and large firms as partners in achieving its goals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In fact, we have statutory provisions in several of our Acts, including the Official Secrets Act, which regulate the collection, use and disclosure of information by the public sector.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As I understand it, privacy impact assessment is just one specific model of ensuring an appropriate balance between individual's expectations of privacy and protection of personal data and public interest.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Ultimately, the public sector is subject to responsibilities that maintain confidentiality and limit the disclosure of personal information, while allowing them to carry out 	Page: 145 their duties.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: All public officials are aware that they have to abide by these rules and we will work with agencies to ensure that they continue to be implemented.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: On the other point that Mr Leon Perera made about how we ensure that there is no digital divide within the Civil Service, we will work with the Civil Service College to conduct a variety of programmes to ensure that civil servants who need the training will be given training opportunities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: There is a whole range of efforts within the Government to ensure that no officers are left behind and that they have the necessary skills to navigate the digital world.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The keen interest in GovTech's work shows that digital Government transformation is an important piece of work and is one that a dedicated agency would be better suited to accomplish.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: The use of ICT provides immense opportunities for improving the delivery of Government services.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: GovTech understands these expectations and I am confident that it will be able to deliver on them to the lives of Singaporeans.      .
